title: Agensh: Scaling Organizational Intelligence to 1,024 Agents
why_read: An interesting empirical study on scaling multi-agent LLM systems to over a thousand concurrent workers without central coordination, with concrete performance numbers on coding benchmarks.
analysis: This paper proposes a fully decentralized multi-agent system where many LLM-driven workers coordinate through shared workspaces and messaging rather than a central orchestrator, aiming to avoid the bottleneck that a single coordinator creates at scale. They test scaling from 1 to 1024 agents on hard coding tasks, reporting substantial improvements in test-pass rates as the number of agents grows, such as raising pandoc task success from about 34% to 55%. This addresses a genuine practical concern in agentic AI systems: how to let many LLM agents work together without a bottlenecked coordinator, and the reported emergent self-organization behavior is intellectually interesting. The results are promising but rely on a specific benchmark and a somewhat unusual GPT-5.6 model naming that warrants some caution about reproducibility and generality.
